# Document the complete DockLayouts feature surface

## Context

The original series reserved a dedicated Features guide. Since then, DockLayouts gained resizable split and edge boundaries, auto-hide rails, perspectives, grouped tab movement and overflow, locking, keyboard behavior, and a default inline action rail with reload, pin, pop-out, maximize, and close.

## The Problem

The current guides explain the architecture and adoption decisions, but not the landed product surface as a coherent reader journey. A developer must search examples, tests, and source to learn what exists, which capabilities are policy-controlled, and which combinations belong together.

## The Architectural Reality

The feature surface spans `Workspace.mjs`, `interaction/{Rail,RevealOverlay,KeyboardCommands,TabSortZone,DockSplitter}.mjs`, projection configuration, perspectives, and host-contributed action/lifecycle hooks. Features share the same committed-document and projection architecture; they are not independent widgets.

## The Fix

Create `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsFeatures.md`: a narrative tour of the complete stabilized feature surface, organized by user outcome and configuration decision rather than a flat checklist.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Feature guide | Current Workspace, interactions, examples, ADR 0029 | Explain supported outcomes and how consumers opt in/configure policy | Do not promise unverified behavior | New guide | Live consumer journeys plus current-source checks |
| Capability claims | Live classes + rendered consumers | Demonstrated outcomes name their receipts; current-source explanations are labelled separately, with honest limits | Never present a source explanation as an observed journey | Same guide | Named consumer receipts and current implementation/ADR checks |
| Registration | Existing guide siblings | One discoverable UI-building-blocks guide | No generated-output edits | tree + SEO inputs | lint + rendered portal |

## Decision Record impact

aligned-with ADR 0029

## Decision Record

Not needed; this guide explains landed capabilities.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guide clears the full guide-authoring bar: source/tool-grounded narrative, reader-owned benefits, lived maintainer voice, and at least one render-verified `flowchart TD`.
- [ ] The guide separates explanation from reference: no inlined API/schema/test catalog, and no ticket or PR ids in guide prose.
- [ ] The new source guide is registered in `learn/tree.json` and the SEO `PRIORITIES` input; generated sitemap/LLM outputs remain untouched.
- [ ] Current-source consistency, guide lint, tree lint, portal rendering, and an independent cross-family whole-guide review are recorded in the PR.
- [ ] The guide covers the stabilized feature families: resizing, tabs/overflow, rails/pin, perspectives, action rail, lock/keyboard, and drag/drop outcomes.
- [ ] Each feature is grounded in current implementation/ADR authority, with capability/policy limits stated. Claims of live demonstration carry a real consumer-action or subsystem-tool receipt; source-explained contracts are explicitly distinguished from demonstrated outcomes.
- [ ] The narrative routes readers to the deeper mechanics, state, window, pane, and styling guides instead of duplicating them.
- [ ] Demonstrated outcomes, current-source contracts not exercised in this guide, and unclaimed/future behavior are explicitly separated.

## Review scope clarification

PR #18700 R1 allowed accurate source-contract explanation in place of invented live-demonstration claims. As the original ticket author, I am aligning the evidence rows and AC-6/AC-8 with that accepted distinction: the guide still covers every feature family, but does not claim it exercised every family on one example page. This supersedes the original all-features-live-demonstrated wording and adds no execution evidence. The public review records the concrete receipts and their limits.

## Out of Scope

An API/config reference table, roadmap checklist, or implementation change.

## Avoided Traps

Do not write a marketing matrix, call a hidden action unsupported, infer support from a class name alone, or present a source explanation as a live journey.

## Activation Gate

Do not author the guide while #17836 remains an active refactoring authority. At pickup, re-run Memory Core mining, read the current ADR 0029 and source/test surfaces named below, exercise the relevant live subsystem, and revalidate the proposed guide boundary. If the final API makes this split wrong, reshape this ticket before writing—do not preserve a stale outline.
